newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador reiterates 96-97 coffee crop outlook.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador reiterates 96-97 coffee crop outlook.

text.p: El Salvador's 1996-1997 coffee crop is still seen ending down 5.0 percent over last cycle at 3.06 million 46-kg bags, the executive director of the Salvadoran Coffee Council said Thursday.

Ruben Pineda told Reuters that the crop prediciton remained the same and was based on technical details and information in his hands from the Salvadoran Foundation for Coffee Investigation, known as Procafe.
"The forecast for the crop is the same given the technical information we have," Pineda said.
The crop outlook includes a 5.0 percent loss of coffee in the current cycle because of rains that damaged trees early in 1996, he added.
Pineda said the study was carried out in 16,000 farms throughout the country.
He said that so far in the current 1996-1997 cycle, more than 70 percent of beans have been harvested.
But the chairwoman of Salvadoran Coffee Association, the country's producer group, disagreed.
Elena Bolanos said the crop this cycle would be down 300,000 46-kg bags over the previous cycle. She did not give a percentage decline for her prediction.
El Salvador's output for 1995-1996 was around 3.2 milion 46-kg bags, which would mean Bolanos was estimating this cycle's production to dip below 3 million bags.
She said winds and rain had caused the dip in production, especially affecting the high-altitude coffee growing regions.
